claims.text: Optimizing the laser scanning strategy improves the dimensional precision of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components by more than 5% relative to conventional additive manufacturing.
Optimizing the laser scanning strategy improves the mechanical integrity of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components by more than 10% relative to conventional additive manufacturing.
Optimizing the laser scanning strategy reduces fabrication-induced defects to below 20% relative to the stated baseline.
The optimized laser scanning strategy alters microstructure and porosity, which mediate the predicted improvements.
The optimized laser scanning strategy reduces thermal gradients during additive manufacturing.
The optimized laser scanning strategy reduces residual stresses in the fabricated components.
Reduced thermal gradients and residual stresses lead to improved dimensional precision and mechanical integrity and to fewer defects.
The predicted effects apply when high-entropy-alloy powder is processed under controlled atmosphere and temperature.
The hypothesis is limited to high-entropy alloys with specific compositions.
